supersededBy: terminal-e2e-verification.json: direct UI-thread callbacks replace broadcast/queue scheduling

architecture.pty: Only updates its Alacritty grid and revision; no VSync subscription or GPU access
architecture.vsync: macOS CADisplayLink on the UI main run loop drives the SDK custom monitor; Rust FrameClock registers native RAF on BTS and publishes to a global tokio broadcast
architecture.listeners: C++ registers Rust FrameListener receivers; window/generation filtering and lifetime stay in Rust
architecture.presentation: Native UI task consumes frame ticks, renders the latest grid into Lynx IOSurface, waits for GPU completion, swaps and completes the Rust frame task
architecture.javascript: No requestAnimationFrame, cancellation, main-thread ref or per-frame renderFrame invocation

checks.napi: Default shell, PTY output, numeric sessions and release passed
checks.runtime_registration: Temporary native tracing observed extension foreground, observer attach, active Rust listener and native RAF registration; tracing code was removed
checks.runtime_automatic_presentation: Passed on an unlocked Mac: initial default-shell prompt and subsequent PTY printf output appeared automatically, including Chinese text. No manual renderFrame was invoked.
checks.runtime_screenshot: Lynx view.takeScreenshot on #application-layout returned data, width=2240, height=1520; its PNG includes the custom native terminal surface. Saved as terminal-native-vsync.png.

runtime_fix: The default macOS VSync monitor produced no callbacks even after unlocking, including Lynx BTS requestAnimationFrame. Official SDK source adds its display link to the current BTS NSRunLoop; registering a custom monitor on the UI main run loop restored frame callbacks.
scope: Verified on macOS arm64 with Lynxtron 0.0.28. Older macOS versions retain the SDK fallback and were not runtime-tested.
